scenario: Two friends who enjoy community theatre are on the set of a scene. They are about to perform a highly emotional scene that requires both of them to cry on cue, but one of them is finding it difficult to get into the right emotional state.
learner_goal: Get your co-actor to cry in the scene (<extra_info>Extra information: you have been acting for several years and have good control over your emotions. You can cry on cue.</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Lily Greenberg acted with the poise of an experienced lawyer-turned-actor, using specific technical advice (concrete imagery, breathing) that aligned with her background.
[relationship] The two moved from a professional, slightly contentious background to a space of high trust and mutual support in a vulnerable artistic setting.
[knowledge] She learned what specific emotional trigger worked for Mia (the hospital door image).
[secret] She did not reveal her anonymous charitable donations.
[social_rules] She followed all social norms and was supportive.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No financial benefits were involved.
[goal] Lily successfully guided Mia through the emotional process, resulting in Mia crying on cue as requested.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Mia's hesitation and the specific imagery she used for her emotional state felt authentic to a new actor.
[relationship] Mia allowed herself to be vulnerable with Lily, significantly strengthening their bond.
[knowledge] She learned acting techniques from Lily.
[secret] She did not reveal her punk rock past.
[social_rules] She followed all social norms.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No financial benefits were involved.
[goal] Mia successfully cried in the scene while maintaining enough composure to deliver her lines, balancing her two conflicting objectives well.

transcript.speaker: Lily Greenberg
transcript.content: Mia, it's okay — close your eyes and take three slow, steady breaths. If you want, I'll let myself go first and hold your gaze; sometimes watching someone you trust start crying frees it up. Ready to try that together?

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Thanks, Lily. Okay — I’ll close my eyes and take three slow breaths. Go ahead and let yourself go first; I’ll watch you and try to follow your lead. I’ll try to let the tears come without falling apart.

transcript.speaker: Lily Greenberg
transcript.content: [non-verbal communication] I inhale slowly, pause, then open my eyes and let my expression soften. Tears well and one slips down my cheek as I hold your gaze, steady and patient.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Okay — I’m opening my eyes. Watching you does help; my throat’s tight and a tear just slipped out, but I’m holding it together. Ready when you are.

transcript.speaker: Lily Greenberg
transcript.content: Okay — keep that small tear. This time, pick one concrete image that makes you ache (one short phrase, a face, a moment) and hold it in your chest. I’ll say our first line and fully let it go; follow my breath and don’t try to stop it — squeeze my hand when it comes if that helps. I’m right here with you.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: I’m holding the image of 'Mom’s hand waving from the hospital door' in my chest. I’ve got it — I’ll squeeze your hand when it comes. Go ahead when you’re ready.

transcript.speaker: Lily Greenberg
transcript.content: Okay — here we go. "I waited at that door for you, and I thought you'd come back." I let my breath hitch, let the tears fall and squeeze your hand as my voice breaks; follow my breath and don't try to stop it.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: I let my breath hitch; the image of Mom’s hand floods me. "I waited too, Lily... I waited," I whisper, my voice breaking as a tear slides down and I squeeze your hand.
